title: AI-Augmented Scientific Workflow Framework
description: Presents a structured framework for integrating Large Language Models into scientific research workflows while maintaining human control, accountability, and scientific integrity. Formalizes four core mechanisms—Question Architecture, Entropy Navigation, Reflective Scaffolding, and Strict Separation of Roles—to support reproducible, transparent, and traceable research.

key_results.main_finding: Formalizes a four-mechanism framework (QA, EN, RS, SR) that enables AI-augmented scientific research while preserving full human epistemic authority, reproducibility, and FAIR-aligned traceability.

kill_criteria: KC1: Framework fails to maintain traceable provenance — if AI-assisted outputs cannot be version-controlled and checksum-verified, the reproducibility guarantee is broken.
KC2: Human validation gate is bypassed — if any scientific claim reaches publication without passing human interpretive authority, the SR mechanism has failed.
KC3: Reflective Scaffolding produces conclusions not grounded in external formal systems (causal models, state machines, schema constraints), invalidating the RS mechanism.
KC4: Framework is shown to systematically amplify hallucination or algorithmic bias rather than mitigating it, contradicting its stated risk-management purpose.
